name: Patchline Gutter Cinch Belt
description:
A hand-assembled utility belt built from salvaged conveyor webbing, reclaimed buckle hardware, and mismatched loop-rivet sets. The strap is a patchwork of black, rust-orange, and industrial grey — no two belts identical. Grease staining on the inner face is common; wearers treat it as proof of use.

Six external loops accommodate tools, zip-pouches, or scavenged containers. The main clasp is a double-tongue steel buckle recovered from old rail harness stock. Crude but reliable.
functionality: Six load-bearing loops for tools or pouches; double-tongue buckle withstands heavy lateral pull; aug-compatible with wide-gap loop spacing to clear lower-limb chrome mounting flanges.
what_it_says: You build what you need from whatever the city discards.
story_hooks: A specific buckle stamp matches decommissioned MagRail maintenance harness — someone is looking for the rig it came from.
The belt's hidden inner seam contains a flattened data chip sewn in by a previous owner.
A Shelf enforcer recognizes the loop pattern as belonging to a missing person.
